thread:
incbot: INCIDENT ALERT: spike in 5xx on inference-api-prod gateway (02:14 UTC). Error rate jumped from ~0.3% -> ~7.8% across region-us-west. Autoretry/threshold fired, paging oncall.

oncall_jordan: acked. I'm on it — paging SRE and runtime. tagging @sre_maya @eng_runtime_lee

sre_maya: looking at the dashboard... seeing correlated latency increase and model-runner pod crashes with OOM+segfaults. tailing logs now.

eng_runtime_lee: I see repeated logs: `model-runner[pid]: segfault at 0x7f...` right after `kv_cache->evict()` on quantized-attention path. Likely regression from the last quant rollout.

pg_ops_olivia: rolling traffic away from us-west->canary routing to reduce load, will also spin up two extra dedicated runners in region for fallback.

oncall_jordan: action plan: 1) enable fallback model (non-quant) for the affected route, 2) scale dedicated pool + remove canary, 3) reduce max-concurrency per runner to limit footprint. @eng_runtime_lee can you flip fallback?

eng_runtime_lee: done — toggled route `inference.v1.generate` -> model: redwood/bert-small:stable-nonquant (fallback). Pushed config at 02:18 UTC. Also reverted quant rollout on the candidate tag.

sre_maya: executed: `infra-cli pool scale --cluster us-west --pool inference-dedicated --delta 2` (02:19 UTC). Also applied `max_concurrency: 6` on the node group.

support_ana: initial customer check: error rate impacting ~1.9% of requests overall. Two Dedicated customers (acct: acme-corp, acct: finpulse) report elevated error rates ~12% in the timeframe. Notified customer success.

pg_ops_olivia: started draining the canary nodes with `kubectl cordon/evict` on pods matching label `quant-rollout=true`.

eng_runtime_lee: posted quick debug snippet for SRE:
```
# recent crash trace
# signal 11 at 0x7f1234
backtrace:
  run_attention_quant+0x234
  kv_cache_evict+0x98
  model_forward+0x1ab
```
Suggest we disable the quant attention kernel until we push fix.

sre_maya: metrics update: 5xx rate falling — now ~0.8% (02:25 UTC). Latency back to baseline on fallback.

oncall_jordan: good. I'm doing a soft handoff to night oncall in 30m. Documenting what we did:
- root cause: crash in quantized attention path causing segfault/OOM during eviction under bursty long-sequence workload.
- mitigations: route switched to non-quant fallback, scaled dedicated pool + lowered concurrency, drained canary pods, revert quant rollout.
- customer impact: ~2% of requests affected, two customers with noticeable errors. CS alerted.

pm_ravi: filing a postmortem ticket and assigning to eng-runtime + quant team for immediate fix + test coverage. Also request: add synthetic long-sequence load test to CI to catch this.

support_ana: customers notified with interim status and ETA for fix requested. Will push updates if they report ongoing errors.

eng_runtime_lee: next steps for us: reproduce locally with quant kernel + long seq, add guard in kv_cache_evict, prepare hotfix for quant kernel (possible bounds check). ETA for patch: ~6-8 hours.

oncall_jordan: final check 02:29 UTC — 5xx steady at 0.4%, no new crashes observed. I'll leave the incident thread open until night handoff. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

sre_maya: leaving notes in PagerDuty runbook and adding trace links. Passing to night oncall: @oncall_lee-night (handoff note).

oncall_jordan: handing off at 02:44 UTC to night oncall: mitigations in place, monitoring OK, followups assigned to eng-runtime.

support_ana: closing customer-facing alert as mitigated, will reopen if errors recur.

incbot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status changed to "mitigated" (02:46 UTC). Continue monitoring; postmortem required.
